papers.title: Probabilistic Fourier extension and the Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract: We give applications of the probabilistic Fourier extension theorem for the paraboloid in d dimensions (see [Saw7] for the sphere, and the proof there holds for a smooth compact piece of the paraboloid) to the global initial value problem for the Schr\"odinger equation with initial data f, in which we obtain sharp averaged Sobolev regularity results over certain `martingale transforms' of the intial data f. The deterministic analogue in three dimensions has been obtained recently by OpenAI [Ope].

papers.title: Asymptotic gradient regularity for degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equations
papers.abstract: This is a continuation of our recent work~\cite{WZJ26} on asymptotic gradient regularity for nonlinear parabolic equations. In this paper, we consider bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*} u_t-|Du|^\gamma F(D^2u)=f \quad \text{in } Q_1, \end{equation*} where $ \gamma>-1 $, $ F $ is uniformly $ (\lambda, \Lambda)$-elliptic with $0<\lambda\leq\Lambda$, $F(0)=0$, and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $ \varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,\alpha)>0 $ such that \[ |\gamma|+\left(\frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}-1\right) \leq \varepsilon \quad \Longrightarrow \quad u \in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+\alpha,\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient H\"older exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $1$ as $ (\gamma, \frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}) \to (0,1) $. This provides a fully nonlinear counterpart to the asymptotic gradient regularity result established in~\cite{WZJ26}.

papers.title: Semialgebraic ${C^m}$ solutions to a univariate system of linear inequalities with Nash forcing
papers.abstract: Let $(A_{ij}(x))_{1 \leq i \leq N, 1 \leq j \leq M}$ be a matrix of univariate semialgebraic functions. We study the solvability of the system of linear inequalities \begin{equation*} \sum_{j=1}^M A_{ij}(x)F_j(x)\leq f_i(x) \ \ \text{ for } i = 1, \ldots, N, \end{equation*} where we assume each forcing $f_i$ is a Nash function. We show that the $C^m$ solvability of the system can be characterized by finitely many linear ordinary differential inequalities in $f$ with semialgebraic coefficients depending only on $(A_{ij})$. When the system is solvable, the solution may be chosen semialgebraic, and the proof gives a constructive procedure in the semialgebraic sense. We also study the semimodule structure of admissible forcings, establishing finite generation and lack thereof in various settings.

papers.title: Folding to the Bessel-Clifford system, and Equivariant Topological Recursion
papers.abstract: We study the interplay between symmetry reductions of meromorphic connections, folding, and topological recursion. As a motivating example, we realize the Bessel-Clifford system as a folding of a symmetry-invariant subspace of the $0-$member of the Painlev\'e IV hierarchy. We introduce equivariant topological recursion for spectral curves with a Klein four-group $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry and prove that the corresponding equivariant correlators can be folded to the ordinary topological recursion correlators on the quotient spectral curve. We further establish the compatibility of this folding with the associated wave functions and quantum curves. In the Bessel-Clifford example, this yields an explicit relation between the equivariant and folded wave functions and recovers the corresponding quantum curve reduction. These results provide a framework for relating symmetry reductions of integrable systems to folding operations in topological recursion.

papers.title: Improved $L^p$ maximal estimates for higher-degree Weyl sums
papers.abstract: For each integer $k\ge3$, we establish the following estimate for all $1\le p<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$: \[ \left\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{n=1}^N e(nx+n^kt)\right|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb{T})} \ll_{k,p,\varepsilon} N^{\max\{1-1/K_k,\,1-1/p\}+\varepsilon}, \] where $K_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k+1)/2\}$, $e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}$, and $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For $k\ge5$, this improves our earlier bound \cite{chen-miao-yuan-zhao} for $1\le p<D_k$, where $D_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k-1)\}$, and, together with the corresponding lower bound, extends the sharp range up to $N^\varepsilon$ from $p\ge D_k$ to $p\ge K_k$. The main new ingredient is a mixed minor-arc moment estimate obtained before taking the time supremum. The minor-arc maximal estimate then follows from a smooth reproducing kernel argument, while the major arcs are handled directly by Poisson summation and classical complete exponential-sum estimates. The reduction from suprema to mean values also yields a short and direct proof of improved $L^p$ estimates for maximal operators on Weyl sums with general polynomial phases, strengthening \cite[Theorem 1.1]{baker-chen-shparlinski}.

papers.title: Ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials
papers.abstract: We introduce ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials, a convexity-enhanced subclass of G\aa{}rding polynomials whose G{\aa}rding components are recursively convex under partial differentiation. This class strictly contains real stable polynomials and, after translation and homogenization, lies in the Lorentzian class. Our main result is that ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials still admit a robust structure theory despite this additional convexity: they are preserved under polarization, satisfy natural closure properties, and support a linear preserver theory. A key contribution of this paper is a universal model for univariate G{\aa}rding polynomials, described by monotone root sequences and equivalently by volume polynomials of Pitman--Stanley polytopes. We establish quotient concavity, and Newton--Maclaurin type inequalities, which leads to the polarization theorem, and suggests further connections with convex geometry and Lorentzian polynomials.

papers.title: Cross-ratios and first order ordinary differential equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the usefulness of the cross-ratio in the study of first order odes of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K,\;n\geqslant1$, where $K$ is a differential field of characteristic zero with algebraically closed field of constants. We discover along the way many differential algebraic identity between solutions to that equation. We also explain why the cross-ratio of any four solutions to such an equation is in general not constant when $n\geq3$ by exhibiting an obstruction which prevents its constancy when $n\geq3$. Finally to any separable polynomial $P_\varphi(z)=z^{n+1}+\varphi_1z^n+\varphi_2z^{n-1}+\ldots+\varphi_{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, over a differential field of meromorphic function on some domain of $\mathbb C$ with the usual derivation we associate a uniquely defined first order ode of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K$ such that every root of $P_\varphi(z)$ is a solution to the said differential equation.

papers.title: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
papers.abstract: For each $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous planar iterated function system of similarities satisfying the strong separation condition, whose attractor $E_\alpha$ has positive finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure and, for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$, satisfies $\sup_{0\le\theta<\pi}H^1(\pi_\theta(N_\delta(E_\alpha)))\lesssim_\alpha(\log\delta^{-1})^{-\alpha}$. The defining system depends only on $\alpha$ and is fixed at every scale. For these same sets, we prove the sharp analytic capacity law $\gamma(N_\delta(E_\alpha))\asymp_\alpha(\log\delta^{-1})^{-1/2}$ as $\delta\rightarrow0$. Consequently, each $E_\alpha$ satisfies the quantitative Vitushkin comparison $\operatorname{Fav}(N_\delta(E_\alpha))\lesssim_\alpha\gamma(N_\delta(E_\alpha))^{2\alpha}$ for every $\delta\in(0,1)$. These comparisons are superlinear for $\alpha>1/2$, with exponents arbitrarily close to the optimal upper limit two for this class of self-similar sets. A completely specified sixteen-map system gives $\alpha=53/100$ and comparison exponent $53/50$. Inspired by Falconer's Venetian blind constructions, the projection argument combines exact collinear cylinder subfamilies, quantitative distribution of word orientations, and a cover indexed by first successful symbolic blocks. The rotation parameters are explicit powers of a real algebraic number, linking the construction to simultaneous Diophantine approximation. The capacity estimate follows from the curvature characterization of analytic capacity and a telescoping inequality for cylinder masses.

papers.title: Integer Parameter Shifts in One-Variable Restrictions of Lauricella's $F_C$
papers.abstract: We construct rational functions of the coefficient index for one-variable restrictions of Lauricella's function $F_C$ at arguments related by cube roots of unity, with arbitrary integer differences among the lower parameters. We express the product coefficients in each residue class as these rational functions times the coefficients of Henrici's known triple product. We obtain finite sums of ordinary ${}_8F_7$ functions whose lower parameters have positive real part, with each summand multiplied by a nonnegative integer power of the variable, and give an explicit formula when the first of three equal lower parameters is increased by one, together with bounds for the polynomial degrees and number of summands. We interpret the expressions for the three residue classes by taking limits of the entire summands when upper and lower parameters approach singular values together. We prove that the Taylor series has radius of convergence exactly $1/4$ whenever all original lower and upper parameters avoid nonpositive integers, without assuming integer differences among the lower parameters.

papers.title: Stieltjes-generated moment functionals and orthogonality: a transfer principle and an image theorem
papers.abstract: We study the orthogonality induced by Stieltjes derivatives from the point of view of ordinary polynomial moment functionals. If \(g\) is a derivator and the Stieltjes monomials \(g_{x_0,n}\) are linearly independent, the map \(\Phi(t^n)=g_{x_0,n}\) is an isomorphism of differential algebras onto the ordinary polynomial algebra, and the intrinsic \(\star\)-bilinear form on \(g\)-polynomials is the pull-back of a single ordinary moment functional \(\mathcal L\). The object of interest is therefore not a new polynomial algebra but the functional generated by the derivator, and our main theorem determines exactly which functionals occur. Let \(c_-\) and \(c_+\) be the increments of the continuous part of \(g\) on the two sides of the centre, and let \(A\) and \(B\) be the multisets of jump sizes to its right and to its left. Then \(\mathcal L\) is Lebesgue measure on \([-c_-,c_+]\), plus an endpoint derivative functional governed by the elementary symmetric functions of \(A\), plus an absolutely continuous left tail whose density is the survival function of a sum of independent exponentials with means in \(B\); the positions of the jumps disappear. Every quadruple \((c_-,c_+,A,B)\) occurs and is recovered from \(\mathcal L\), so the fibres are described exactly, and \(\mathcal L\) is representable by a positive measure precisely when \(|A|\le1\). A weighted lattice extension, in which the transported moments are the factorial moments of the weight, is treated separately.

papers.title: Endpoint Lorentz Inequality for Riesz Potentials with Respect to General Measures
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $\alpha\in(0,n)$, and $\mu$ be a locally finite nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that, for any $f\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$, \begin{align*} \|I_\alpha f\|_{L^{\frac{n}{n-\alpha},1}(\mu)} \le C_{n,\alpha} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} |Rf(x)|[M\mu(x)]^{1-\frac{\alpha}{n}}\,dx, \end{align*} where $I_\alpha$ is the Riesz potential, $R$ is the Riesz transform, $M\mu$ is the Hardy--Littlewood maximal function of $\mu$, and $C_{n,\alpha}$ is a positive constant depending only on $n$ and $\alpha$. This answers a question posed by Bortz, Moen, Olivo, P\'erez, and Rela, with the case $\alpha=1$ already known, and extends Spector's optimal unweighted Lorentz inequality to general measures. As applications, we obtain a Lorentz estimate for curl-free vector fields, Sobolev--Lorentz and Hardy inequalities with respect to general measures, and an $A_1$-weighted Lorentz estimate with a sharp exponent of the $A_1$ characteristic.

papers.title: Quantitative maximal $\mathrm{L}^p$-regularity for generators of real contraction semigroups
papers.abstract: Let $-A$ be the generator of a real, symmetric contraction semigroup on a $\sigma$-finite measure space. We prove a universal bound for maximal $\mathrm{L}^p$-regularity: In space-time norms $$\|Au\|_p \leq \big(p^* + \tfrac{p^*}{2(p^*-1)}\big) \|f\|_p,$$ where $p^* = \max(p,p/(p-1))$ and $u$ is the mild solution to the Cauchy problem with right-hand side $f$ starting at $u(0)=0$. Linear growth of the constant in $p^*$ is optimal. Our proof introduces an elementary approach to maximal regularity that avoids both vector-valued harmonic analysis and dilation theory. We also obtain quantitative maximal regularity estimates for real, non-symmetric semigroups that are contractive on a sector.

papers.title: Disproof of Wright's Problems 14 and 15 on lacunary maximal functions
papers.abstract: We disprove the proposed weak endpoint bounds in James Wright's Problems 14 and 15 from the 2017 collection of harmonic-analysis problems. For every $d\ge1$, we exhibit a fixed compactly supported singular probability measure with Fourier decay of every order $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, for which the dyadic convolution maximal operator has infinite weak $L^1$ and infinite $H^1$ to weak $L^1$ operator norms. For every finite nonempty set of dyadic scales, both optimal weak constants equal the number of scales, with the Hardy constant measured in the specified atomic norm. Increasingly separated renewal digits provide uniform real-frequency Fourier decay while allowing the disjoint output regions needed for the positive and mean-zero tests. We first establish the fixed measure, then prove the two endpoint estimates using separate normalized tests. Finally we prove the two Fourier lemmas used in the construction.

papers.title: Orthonormal maximal estimates for fractional Schr\"odinger operators along H\"older curves
papers.abstract: We establish orthonormal maximal estimates for one-dimensional fractional Schr\"odinger operators along curves that are H\"older continuous in time and bi-Lipschitz in space. For both the convex range $m>1$ and the concave range $0<m<1$, we obtain sharp Sobolev regularity in terms of the order $m$. As an application, we obtain almost everywhere convergence of the associated densities to their initial values along the curves. The proof combines Schatten duality with kernel estimates.

papers.title: Maximal estimates of the Schr\"odinger operators with quadratic potential for orthonormal systems
papers.abstract: We establish an equivalence principle for local mixed-norm estimates for generalized Schr\"odinger propagators acting on orthonormal systems. Under suitable mixed-norm conditions, estimates for generalized propagators follow from the corresponding free Schr\"odinger estimates for every summability exponent $1\le\beta\le2$. Applications include maximal estimates for Schr\"odinger equations with time-dependent quadratic potentials and for the special Hermite operator, as well as almost everywhere convergence of the associated densities. For the special Hermite operator, we also obtain a single-function maximal estimate that is sharp up to the endpoint. We construct counterexamples for the Schr\"odinger operator, by combining single particle and many particle constructions in complementary dimensions, yielding new necessary conditions in an intermediate range of summability exponents.

papers.title: On the asymptotic growth of the norm of the partial sum operator on $\mathscr H^1$
papers.abstract: We show that the norm of the partial sum operator $S_N$ on the Hardy space $\mathscr H^1$ of Dirichlet series satisfies $$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\log N}{\log N}\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\geq\frac{1-\log 2}{2\pi}.$$ Combined with an upper bound of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman and Seip, this shows that $$\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\asymp\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}$$ as $N\to\infty$.

papers.title: Sharp $L^6$ Fourier moments and (3,$\delta$)-energy estimates for fractal measures on the truncated cone in $\R^3$
papers.abstract: For a $\delta$-separated $(\delta,d)$-Katz--Tao set $P$ on the truncated cone in $\R^3$, $1<d\le 2$, we prove the sharp energy bound \[ \E_{3,\delta}(P)\lesssim_{\varepsilon} \delta^{-\varepsilon} \max\{\delta^{-(3d+2)},\delta^{-(5d-1)}\}. \] The proof applies the Fu--Ren incidence theorem to triples with a fixed sum. As a corollary we also deduce a sharp $L^6$ moment estimate for the Fourier transform of Frostman measures supported on the cone.

papers.title: Constructions and reductions on the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations
papers.abstract: We investigate five open problems concerning the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations posed by Marinescu and Niculescu. We give constructive answers to three of them. First, we construct an equivalent norm on $\ell^2$ with no three-dimensional Hornich-Hlawka subspace. Second, we present a Nakano space that is not Hornich-Hlawka. Third, we show that the $\alpha$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $\alpha \in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. This implies that on every nonzero inner product space, the $\alpha$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality holds for all triples precisely when $\alpha \in (0,1] \cup \{2\}$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$. Finally, for $p(\cdot): (0, 1) \to [1, 2]$ measurable and integers $k \geq 0$, we establish a Sobolev-Nakano equivalence: we prove that $W^{k,p(\cdot)}(0,1)$, equipped with the sum of the Luxemburg norms of its derivatives of orders $0, \ldots, k$, is Hornich-Hlawka if and only if $L^{p(\cdot)}(0,1)$ is Hornich-Hlawka.

papers.title: On extremal problems related to the Krzy\.{z} conjecture
papers.abstract: We study general extremal problems similar or closely related to the Krzy\.z conjecture and establish the structural properties of extremal functions, pointing out some differences with the original Krzy\.z case. We also introduce a family of more specific problems of this kind, interpolating between the Krzy\.z problem and the problem of maximizing the constant term, and show that they are closely related to the Krzy\.z conjecture: the conjecture implies the analogous statement for all of them and, conversely, if one of them has the same extremal value as the Krzy\.z problem, then this value is $2/e$. This may represent a new approach to attacking the original problem. Finally, we show that for these problems an extremal function whose Taylor coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ vanish must be the conjectured one; as a special case, we obtain a new proof of a recent result of MacDonald.

papers.title: A Zero--One Law for Subrings of the Reals Closed under Binary Interleaving
papers.abstract: Erd\H{o}s Problem 1154 asks whether every number in $[0,1]$ occurs as the Hausdorff dimension of a subring or subfield of $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that a subring of $\mathbb{R}$ closed under binary interleaving has Hausdorff dimension either zero or one. Consequently, every Turing ideal and its associated subfield satisfy the same dichotomy.

papers.title: Optimal convergence rates for the finite element approximation of the Sobolev constant
papers.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates for the continuous piecewise affine finite element approximation of the Sobolev constant in arbitrary dimensions N\geq 2 and for Lebesgue exponents 1<p<N. Our analysis relies on a refined study of the Sobolev deficit in suitable quasi-norms, which have been introduced and utilized in the context of finite element approximations of the p-Laplacian. The proof further involves sharp estimates for the finite element approximation of Sobolev minimizers.

papers.title: Compactness of bilinear singular integral with mild kernel regularity
papers.abstract: We establish a compact bilinear $T1$ theorem for Calder\'on-Zygmund operators with mild kernel regularity. The exponent obtained here matches the best-known threshold in the sufficient condition for the classical bilinear $T1$ theorem. We also introduce an equivalent unified testing condition WCP$^{*}$.

papers.title: Wave Packet Density in Local Smoothing: Refinements and Limitations
papers.abstract: We study wave packet density estimates in the local smoothing problem for the wave equation. Building on the framework of Gan, He, Li, and Wu, we refine the broad-incidence argument to obtain an improved local smoothing range in even dimensions. We then investigate the limitations of wave packet density methods, showing that genuine geometric obstructions already arise in the Euclidean setting.

papers.title: A Mizohata--Takeuchi-type estimate for the hyperbolic paraboloid
papers.abstract: We prove Mizohata--Takeuchi-type estimates for the Fourier extension operator associated with the truncated hyperbolic paraboloid in $\R^3$. Our main result controls the weighted $L^2$ norm of the extension operator by the $L^2$ mass of the weight over a multiscale family of parallelepipeds arising from $\ell^2$ decoupling for the hyperbolic paraboloid. We deduce this result from a weighted $L^2$ estimate for functions whose Fourier transforms are supported in a small neighborhood of the hyperbolic paraboloid, which we establish using a bilinear refined decoupling estimate.
